goalInOwnWords: Build a little production line out of the parts the cards give me so scrap turns into ingots and reaches the dock. Each shift has an order to fill; fill it and everything sells 25 percent higher for the rest of the job. Fill all six orders for three stars and make more money than Sal.
stoppedWhere: Home screen, after finishing the whole of today's yard (3 stars, $20,295) and then opening a replay of the same yard and a new practice yard (rivet-forge-499) without playing a shift in either; then the survey.
stoppedWhy: I had solved it. The game itself told me a second furnace was the fix, I found a better layout than the one it offered, and from shift 3 on there was nothing left to chase: I beat Sal's $9,157 by more than double and there is no leaderboard. A replay of the same yard would buy me about 2 percent by reordering picks. The new yard had the same six order prices, the same kit and the same Tuner line on a different map, so it would be the same recipe again through fiddly clicking. I am not hungry for another one right now; I would try tomorrow's yard if it gave me a target I cannot double on the first go.

stuck.what: Where my two stars and $9,840 from yesterday had gone: the rank box said 0 stars, 'No finished games yet' and '0 games played on this device'.
stuck.gotOutHow: Opened the small grey 'From earlier versions (v8)' fold-out, which showed 'best $9,840 (yard daily-2026-11-01) - 1 game, kept for the record'. The stars themselves never came back and nothing said why.

stuck.what: How to move a hopper and turn machines. Dragging the hopper one cell left a conveyor behind on the cell it left, a plain click on a machine turned it a quarter turn, and I could not tell what laid the belt.
stuck.gotOutHow: Clicked the stray belt and sent it back to the shelf, then turned machines by repeated clicks. A help line ('Drag parts onto the belt. Drag across empty yard to lay belt. Click a machine to turn or move it...') only appeared when nothing was selected, after I had already worked it out.

stuck.what: Where the second furnace could go. The game had just told me a second furnace behind a Splitter would clear the bottleneck, then every card said 'No easy spot yet' and Sal said 'No card here fits your line yet. New offers deals three more for $40.'
stuck.gotOutHow: Took the Furnace + Splitter card anyway, pulled my hopper and crusher off the cell above the dock, put the new furnace there and re-seated the crusher and hopper beside it. Forecast went from $1,368 to $2,268.

stuck.what: How to give a third furnace an input and an output when the dock had no free side.
stuck.gotOutHow: Clicked the Tuner and read that it carries what a belt carried, so the Tuner already beside the dock could pass shards into a furnace on the dock's free side. Forecast went from $2,646 to $4,200.

confused: Home screen says 0 stars, no finished games and 0 games played, when I finished a game yesterday; the record is only in a tiny 'From earlier versions (v8)' fold-out with a yard code.
The top bar says 'Today's yard . practice' on the real daily yard and 'First try on this yard'; I could not tell if the run counted for anything.
'Lit spots: when you ask' on the job card: is that the current setting or what the button will switch to? I never found out.
Clicking a machine both selects it and rotates it, so I rotated parts I only wanted to look at.
Dragging a hopper one cell left a conveyor behind that I had not asked for.
'No easy spot yet' and 'No card here fits your line yet' on the exact card the game had just told me I needed (a second furnace behind a Splitter), with a $40 re-roll as the suggested fix.
'You're level with Sal. The lit spots are his game: beat him by finding better.' took two readings before I understood the hints are his play.
'From shift 4, plates sell for $42 too' when the price list said Plate $8; a plate costs two shards, so it is worse than an ingot at the same price. No one told me the plate price changes.
'What held you back: The crusher again, for 0 of 80 seconds.' lists a bottleneck that held me back for no seconds.
Last shift said 'You're $11,058 ahead of Sal' and the results said 'You beat Sal by $11,138'; $80 apart for the same number.
Shipping Dock card says 'Gives your line room to grow' but I could not tell what a second dock would do for me.
'Play again' on the results screen does not say whether it replays the same yard or gives a new one (it was the same yard, with the same offers).
annoyed: Rotation only goes clockwise by click or Turn, so facing a machine the other way took up to three clicks, and I did that many times.
Parts often arrived facing the wrong way: a crusher fed the wrong furnace, a furnace faced off the board and dropped the forecast, a tuner faced the wrong machine.
The shelf has seven slots; with more than seven things on it a part is drawn hanging outside the frame.
Sal kept saying 'No easy spot for the Splitter yet. Move a machine to make room.' for parts I had decided not to use; two Splitters sat on the shelf all game.
Yesterday's stars were wiped from the rank (0 stars) and the game never said the rules had changed.
Sal's game on this yard was $9,157 and I made $20,295 with the first good idea; there is no leaderboard, so nothing to chase.
'Order filled. Every price goes up 25%.' on the last shift, when there is no next shift.
Fixing a layout costs many small drags and clicks; the maths is fun, the interface is a chore.
pleased: 'This shift will pay $X' was exact to the dollar every shift (1,005, 1,296, 2,268, 4,200, 5,424, 6,102), so I could plan with it and trust it.
'What shipped' and 'What held you back' after each shift named the true bottleneck ('The furnace held you back for 76 of 80 seconds'), with a red tag on the machine.
The 'What things sell for' fold-out with prices and timings; the numbers added up when I checked them.
Tooltips that state a real rule: 'Nothing feeds the Crusher. It takes things from behind or either side, never head-on.' and 'That's a junk pile. Nothing can stand here: go around it.'
Lit spots only when I ask; no hand-holding unless I want it.
Beating the game's own 'no easy spot' with a layout it did not offer (forecast $1,368 to $2,268).
The Tuner doubling as a conveyor and one Tuner serving two machines.
Seeing next shift's three cards in advance so I can plan a build across shifts.
Three stars and the shift-by-shift bars on the results screen.
bestMoment: Shift 3: the game said there was no easy spot for a second furnace, I pulled my hopper and crusher off the dock, rebuilt the corner by hand, and the forecast jumped from $1,368 to $2,268 and the shift paid exactly that.
worstMoment: Shift 1 build: dragging a hopper one cell left an unrequested belt behind, a click turned a machine I only meant to select, and it took around ten actions to put two parts where I wanted while the help line that explained it was hidden.
oneChange: A real target to chase: a par or leaderboard I cannot double with my first good idea (Sal's $9,157 against my $20,295). Fix the fiddly rotation too, but give me something worth optimising towards.
